claims.claim: Related work spans reproducible computation, research assistants, and autonomous discovery. Systems such as AI Scientist pursue an end-to-end research cycle, particularly in machine learning~\cite{AIScientist,AIResearch2026}, while astronomy applications and perspectives emphasize domain tools and scientific judgment~\cite{Mephisto,TingUnderstanding}. Our contribution is a guide to verifiable human--agent work in physical science, with adversarial review, provenance, and human-guided interpretation and writing. Appendix~\ref{app:related} places these practices alongside current systems, evaluations, and proposals.

claims.claim: \textbf{Reproducibility and agent provenance.} CODECHECK organizes independent execution during review and explicitly separates checking execution from judging the scientific method~\cite{CODECHECK}. PROV-AGENT extends workflow provenance to connect agent prompts, responses, and decisions with downstream computations~\cite{PROVAGENT}. Such records make a result inspectable; they do not make an incorrect calculation correct. Hans and Bilionis's \emph{Paper-replication} implements a related coding-agent skill: selected claims become targets linked to executed evidence, comparisons, and report coverage, with a completion gate~\cite{PaperReplication}. Passing that gate concerns the recorded target set; their repeated runs still differ in numerical fidelity and acceptance rules. These approaches complement our emphasis on generated numerical macros, figure recipes, and adversarial review.

claims.claim: \textbf{Autonomous research in computer science.} AI Scientist automates idea generation, experiments, and manuscript preparation within a supplied research environment; subsequent work develops the end-to-end AI-research program~\cite{AIScientist,AIResearch2026}. Agent Laboratory instead explicitly explores research assistance and human feedback~\cite{AgentLab}. AlphaEvolve evolves executable programs using human-supplied automatic evaluators~\cite{AlphaEvolve}. These are substantive demonstrations, with different scopes of autonomy. A machine-evaluable objective provides a particularly effective feedback loop, but the choice and scientific adequacy of that objective remain consequential. Our guide addresses how scientists make the resulting work verifiable and interpretable; it does not claim to demonstrate autonomous discovery.

claims.claim: \textbf{Domain science and human validation.} Agentic systems also support domain science with differing human roles. Mephisto applies an agent to physical-component selection in galaxy spectral-energy-distribution modeling, using a domain code, structured diagnostics, and accumulated experience~\cite{Mephisto}. Co-Scientist generates and debates biological hypotheses, with experts selecting candidates and conducting experimental validation~\cite{CoScientist}. Kosmos combines literature search and data analysis, with traceable reports and sampled expert checks that distinguish analysis, literature, and synthesis claims~\cite{Kosmos}. Those distinctions matter: a retrieved citation, a reproduced calculation, and a plausible interpretation require different checks. Ting's hands-on astronomy course provides a complementary teaching route through tool execution, retrieval, agent memory, and safety~\cite{TingCourse}; it is instructional material rather than a performance study.

claims.claim: \textbf{What an evaluation measures.} PaperBench evaluates replication of machine-learning research using graded implementation and execution evidence~\cite{PaperBench}. ReplicationBench uses expert-designed astrophysics tasks to assess both methodological faithfulness and correctness~\cite{ReplicationBench}. These test a broader task than finding a defect in an existing workflow. Their results depend on the dated model, harness, resources, and scoring rule; they are not measurements of the current frontier-model review capability described in this guide. Conversely, successful error diagnosis does not establish that an agent can independently choose and complete an important research program. ARA addresses another task: assessing reconstructability from the manuscript, without executing its code~\cite{ARA}. Document assessment and demonstrated reruns must remain distinguishable.

claims.claim: \textbf{Fast-moving practice and proposals.} First-party engineering reports can document useful procedures before journal publication. Anthropic describes bounded delegation, evidence handling, and evaluation in a multi-agent web-research system~\cite{AnthropicResearch}; these observations concern its own system. OpenAI, PerturbAI, and Scripps report a recent large-scale analysis of biological data yielding candidate leads~\cite{OpenAIBiology}. Such leads should be distinguished from experimentally validated mechanisms. At the architectural level, Traxia proposes verifiable agent-native publishing, but explicitly presents a specification and partial prototype without empirical validation~\cite{Traxia}. These sources identify active directions rather than establish that a proposed safeguard works. The recurring practical question for this guide is what evidence another scientist can inspect and challenge.
